definitions.explanation: The Celsius temperature scale, in which water freezes at 0 degrees and boils at 100 degrees. Japan uses the Celsius scale for all temperature measurements in daily life, weather, and science.

examples.japanese: ⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{摂氏|せっし}100⟦{度|ど}→〜度：09845_do⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{沸騰|ふっとう}する→沸騰する：21985_futtousuru⟧。

⟦アメリカ→アメリカ：01769_amerika⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{華氏|かし}→華氏：28130_kashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{使|つか}われる→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{摂氏|せっし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{標準|ひょうじゅん}→標準：04832_hyoujun⟧⟦である→である：09855_dearu⟧。
examples.english: Fahrenheit is used in America, but Celsius is the standard in Japan.

notes:
USAGE:
Named after the Chinese transliteration of Anders Celsius ({摂爾修斯|セルシウス}). In everyday Japanese, temperatures are almost always given in Celsius without explicitly saying {摂氏|せっし} — people simply say 30⟦{度|ど}→〜度：09845_do⟧ (30 degrees). The word {摂氏|せっし} is used when explicitly distinguishing from Fahrenheit or in scientific contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {摂氏|せっし}〜⟦{度|ど}→〜度：09845_do⟧: ~ degrees Celsius
- {摂氏|せっし}⟦{温度|おんど}→温度：00333_ondo⟧: Celsius temperature

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{華氏|かし}→華氏：28130_kashi⟧: Fahrenheit (the counterpart scale used in the US)
